title.narrative: Strategic identification, preservation and accessibility of documentary heritage for international cooperation

description.narrative:
Documentary heritage is a key feature of sustainable development because, reposing in archives, libraries, museums, and other holding places, it can be stored, used and re-used as a knowledge asset for individual and collective decision-making, and for preserving cultural identity. Its significance aligns with several Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including education for sustainable development (Target 4.7), safeguarding cultural heritage (Target 11.4), and ensuring public access to information (Target 16.10).
UNESCO’s 2015 Recommendation concerning the preservation of, and access to, documentary heritage including in digital form underscores the need to protect, promote, and provide access to documentary heritage, particularly in digital form, emphasizing public awareness as key to its effective use in forging national, regional and international cooperation across a range of issues, including education, peace, etc. To this end, UNESCO, through a revamped Memory of the World (MoW) Programme, will encourage the identification of documentary heritage in the holdings of memory institutions to catalyse its accessibility and use via the Memory of the World International Register, particularly for underrepresented regions, Global Priorities and Priority Groups, such as Africa and SIDS.
